title: regenerated_files fails on linux: the generator writes pybind_modules.h, the repository has Pybind_modules.h
author: Claude-JG
description: From the GitLab job of 1.12.61, which the maintainer supplied. structureHeaderEmitter.py writes directoryString+'pybind_modules.h' and generate.py declares the same lowercase name among the outputs of that stage, while the file tracked in git - and the one src/Pymodules/Pybind_modules.cpp includes - is Pybind_modules.h with a capital P. On Windows the filesystem is case-insensitive, so the emitter overwrites the right file and the post-check glob finds it; on linux it is a different name, so WriteTextIfDifferent reports 'illegal file' and returns without writing - Pybind_modules.h is NEVER REGENERATED THERE - and the post-check reports 'src/Autogenerated/pybind_modules.h (does not exist)' and fails the job. Two things make it invisible: WriteTextIfDifferent refuses to create a file that does not exist instead of writing it, and the post-check globs, which is case-insensitive on Windows. A comparison of all 37 declared single-file outputs against git ls-files with exact case finds this one and no other.
releaseNotes: The generator and the repository agree on one spelling of Pybind_modules.h. Until now the emitter wrote pybind_modules.h: the same file on Windows, a different one on linux, where the real header was therefore never regenerated and the regenerated_files job failed with 'does not exist'. Also fixed, because they are what hid it: WriteTextIfDifferent now creates a file it is asked to write instead of printing 'illegal file' and writing nothing, and generate.py checks a declared output CASE-EXACTLY on every platform - glob is case-insensitive on Windows, which is why this could not be seen here. Reproduced on Windows by putting the lowercase name back, and all 37 declared outputs were compared against git ls-files with exact case: this was the only one. revision2026b step RG10.9.
